metaTitle: Clogged Drain Cleaning in Glendale, CA | Cost & Causes
metaDescription: Slow or blocked drain in your Glendale home? Learn what causes it, what a plumber does, and the real cost ($135–$315) before you call.
intro: A slow-draining sink or tub in Glendale often points to more than just hair or grease buildup — the city's older mid-century apartment plumbing and hillside home foundations can add extra wrinkles to a simple clog. If water is backing up, gurgling, or draining slower each day, it's worth understanding what's really going on before it turns into a bigger mess.
causes: Hair, soap scum, and grease building up inside bathroom or kitchen drain lines over time.
Tree roots infiltrating older clay or cast-iron sewer lines, which are still common in Glendale's mid-century apartment buildings.
Ground settling or shifting on hillside properties, which can cause pipe bellies or misalignment that trap debris.
Mineral and scale buildup inside galvanized pipes found in many pre-1970s Glendale homes.
Foreign objects or excess toilet paper flushed into a line with an already narrow diameter.
whatProDoes: Runs a camera inspection or uses a drain snake to locate the clog and identify its cause.
Clears the blockage using a motorized auger, hydro-jetting, or hand tools depending on pipe material and clog severity.
Checks nearby fixtures and cleanouts to confirm water is flowing freely through the full line.
Flags any signs of root intrusion, pipe damage, or bellying that may need further repair, especially relevant on sloped hillside lots.
Tests the drain again under normal use to make sure the clog hasn't just been pushed further down the line.
diyOrPro: A single slow sink you can plunge or treat with a basic hand snake is reasonable to try yourself. But if multiple drains are backing up at once, water is coming up from a floor drain, or you're on a hillside lot with older sewer lines, that points to a deeper blockage or a shifted pipe — call a plumber rather than risk sewage backup or working blind on a line you can't see.
priceNote: This job runs $135 to $315 in Glendale, based on a $94 hourly rate and jobs typically taking 1 to 3 hours. Simple fixture clogs land at the lower end, while main line blockages, root intrusion, or hard-to-reach pipes in older buildings push the job toward the higher end.

faqs.q: Why does my drain keep clogging even after I clear it myself?
faqs.a: Repeat clogs often mean the blockage is further down the line than a plunger or store-bought snake can reach, or there's a structural issue like root intrusion or a pipe belly — common in Glendale's older sewer lines. A plumber with a camera can find the actual cause instead of just treating the symptom.

faqs.q: Is a clogged drain ever a sign of a bigger problem in a hillside home?
faqs.a: Yes. Ground movement on sloped lots can shift or crack pipes over time, creating low spots where debris collects. If a drain clogs repeatedly in the same spot, it's worth having a plumber check for pipe damage rather than just clearing it again.

faqs.q: Why would a drain cleaning cost closer to $315 instead of $135?
faqs.a: The price depends on how long the job takes. A simple sink clog might clear in about an hour, but a main line blockage, tree root intrusion, or a clog in hard-to-access older plumbing can take up to three hours to fully clear, which moves the cost toward the higher end of the range.
